1	---
2	tags: [architecture, people-hub, directus]
3	---
4	
5	## People hub: schema and permission model
6	
7	Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
8	hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
9	deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.
10	
11	### Scope and non-goals
12	
13	- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
14	  the camp schedule (programs/sessions/classes/capacity), and registrations. No household
15	  grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household, only per-registration guardians and emergency
16	  contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
17	- Terminology matches Clubspot and the website: **program** (Clubspot's `Camp`), **session**
18	  (`CampSession`), **class** (`CampClass`), **registration** (`Registration`/`RegistrationCampSession`)
19	  — not "enrollment."
20	- Registration status and person contact fields get **history, not just a current value** — see
21	  [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance).
22	- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
23	  below.
24	- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
25	  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.
26	
27	### Collections
28	
29	**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
30	contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
31	Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
32	participant from a `registrations` row (see [Collections](#collections) below).
33	
34	No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
35	contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
36	and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
37	problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.
38	
39	| Field                     | Type                                              | Notes                               |
40	| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
41	| `id`                      | uuid                                              | primary key                         |
42	| `first_name`, `last_name` | string                                            |                                     |
43	| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable                                  | contact info, not auth              |
44	| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable                                    | required for minors                 |
45	| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |
46	
47	**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
48	can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
49	contact).
50	
51	| Field                                    | Type                        | Notes                                             |
52	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
53	| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
54	| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
55	| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |
56	
57	**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
58	emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
59	relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
60	one's `relationship_type` enum.
61	
62	Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
63	guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
64	(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
65	is what recovers Clubspot's primary-vs-secondary guardian distinction once #70 turns those flat
66	fields into rows here.
67	
68	| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                     |
69	| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
70	| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                               |
71	| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                 |
72	| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact         |
73	| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                           |
74	| `contact_order`     | integer                                | call order when a minor has more than one |
75	
76	**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
77	(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
78	[Permission model](#permission-model).
79	
80	| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
81	| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
82	| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
83	| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
84	| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
85	
86	**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
87	(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.
88	
89	| Field              | Type                     | Notes                                                                          |
90	| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
91	| `id`               | uuid                     | primary key                                                                    |
92	| `name`             | string                   |                                                                                |
93	| `category`         | string, nullable         | Clubspot's own grouping (e.g. "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Adult Sailing") |
94	| `clubspot_camp_id` | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                                                              |
95	
96	**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).
97	
98	| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
99	| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
100	| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
101	| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
102	| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
103	| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |
104	
105	**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.
106	"Advanced"). Each registration entry is for a specific session _and_ class — see
107	`registration_entries` below.
108	
109	| Field               | Type                      | Notes                                                                  |
110	| ------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
111	| `id`                | uuid                      | primary key                                                            |
112	| `program_id`        | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` | a class belongs to the program, independent of which sessions offer it |
113	| `name`              | string                    |                                                                        |
114	| `clubspot_class_id` | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70                                                      |
115	
116	**session_classes** — which classes a session actually offers, i.e. the camp schedule itself. A
117	pure join, no fields of its own. Denormalized: Clubspot represents this as either an explicit
118	`CampSession.campClassesArray` or an `allClasses` flag meaning "every class in the program" — #70's
119	sync expands the `allClasses` case into one row per program class at sync time, so this table always
120	holds the actual explicit list and nothing downstream needs to special-case the flag. No Clubspot id
121	of its own — it's an array (or a flag) on `CampSession`, not a separate object — so #70 just
122	reconciles rows to match Clubspot's current state each sync (remove rows no longer present, add new
123	ones).
124	
125	| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
126	| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
127	| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
128	| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
129	| `class_id`   | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`  |             |
130	
131	**entry_caps** — capacity, matching Clubspot's `EntryCap` exactly: a cap on one class, either
132	overall (`session_id` null, applies across every session) or for one specific session.
133	
134	| Field                   | Type                                | Notes                                            |
135	| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
136	| `id`                    | uuid                                | primary key                                      |
137	| `class_id`              | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`            |                                                  |
138	| `session_id`            | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`, nullable | null = applies to this class across all sessions |
139	| `cap`                   | integer                             | the actual limit (Clubspot's own field name)     |
140	| `clubspot_entry_cap_id` | string, nullable, unique            | dedup key for #70                                |
141	
142	This — `programs` / `sessions` / `classes` / `session_classes` / `entry_caps` — is the camp
143	schedule: worth capturing accurately from #70's first sync rather than backfilling later, since the
144	website and the eventual financial-model app both need it, not just rosters/permissions.
145	
146	**registrations** — one row per Clubspot `Registration` object: a participant's signup for a
147	program (Clubspot's own term — matched here rather than "enrollment"). This is the parent; a single
148	registration can cover multiple sessions/classes (a multi-week camp signup), which is what
149	`registration_entries` below is for. Billing/payment (Clubspot's `billing_registration`) stays out
150	of scope, same as the rest of the financial model.
151	
152	| Field                      | Type                      | Notes             |
153	| -------------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
154	| `id`                       | uuid                      | primary key       |
155	| `person_id`                | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   | the participant   |
156	| `program_id`               | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
157	| `clubspot_registration_id` | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |
158	
159	**registration_entries** — one row per session + class within a registration (Clubspot's
160	`RegistrationCampSession` — "Session Join Id" in the existing `ParticipantsReport`). A registration
161	spanning multiple weeks/classes becomes multiple entries here, matching what the current spreadsheet
162	already does.
163	
164	| Field                      | Type                                        | Notes                                                                                                                            |
165	| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
166	| `id`                       | uuid                                        | primary key                                                                                                                      |
167	| `registration_id`          | uuid, FK -> `registrations.id`              |                                                                                                                                  |
168	| `session_id`               | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                                                                                                                                  |
169	| `class_id`                 | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`                    |                                                                                                                                  |
170	| `status`                   | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60; the _current_ status — see [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance) for history |
171	| `clubspot_session_join_id` | string, nullable, unique                    | dedup key for #70 (`RegistrationCampSession`'s own id)                                                                           |
172	
173	### Change tracking and provenance
174	
175	Directus already does this: every API-driven create/update/delete is logged in `directus_activity`
176	(who, when, on what) with a paired `directus_revisions` row holding the full item snapshot and a
177	delta — for every collection, no opt-in needed. Architecture.md already assumed this
178	(`Audit — Directus activity log for data access/changes`), so there's no need for bespoke history
179	tables here, as long as #70 always writes through the Directus API (never raw SQL):
180	
181	- **Registration status** (waitlist → confirmed → cancelled) doesn't need its own event log — the
182	  revision history on a `registration_entries` row already shows every state it's been in and when
183	  Directus recorded each change. If Clubspot's own historical timestamps
184	  (`RegistrationCampSession.waitlist_updates`) matter and not just "when we noticed," #70's first
185	  import of a registration can replay each transition as its own sequential write so the revision
186	  _order_ matches reality — though the revision _timestamp_ is always "when Directus saw the write,"
187	  not the original Clubspot moment; a backfill can't inject history at an arbitrary past time.
188	- **Person contact-field changes** (a guardian's email changing between registrations two years
189	  apart) are the same story: the revision history on a `people` row already shows every value
190	  `email`/`phone`/`first_name`/`last_name` has held. Confirmed by looking at the live participants

Backing the people hub (see [docs/people-hub-schema.md](people-hub-schema.md)). No oauth2-proxy in

> (MSCL-licensed) gates behind a paid Enterprise license** — confirmed hands-on while building the
> schema snapshot (a fresh, unlicensed v12.3.1 instance rejected any permission with a `permissions`
> filter with `403 custom_permission_rules_enabled is a restricted resource`; the identical call
> succeeds on v11.17.4). **Pin Directus to a v11.x tag** (`docker-compose.yml` currently pins

      authorized redirect URI `https://crm.cycsail.team/auth/login/google/callback`.
- [ ] Put the client id/secret into `directus-oauth-client-id` / `directus-oauth-client-secret` (§3).
- [ ] Consent screen can be the same **External** app as the portal's, or its own — either works, as
      long as the redirect URI above is registered on whichever client Directus is given.

### 6.2 Database role — Cloud SQL

Pulumi declares the `directus` database (`database.ts`) but not its Postgres role/password — same
"container only, value out of band" split as every other secret here.

- [ ] Connect to the `substrate` Cloud SQL instance (`gcloud sql connect substrate --user=postgres`,
      or via a bastion/IAP tunnel) and create the role Directus connects as:
      ```sql
      CREATE USER directus WITH PASSWORD 'the same value stored in directus-db-password (§3)';
      GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE directus TO directus;
      ```

### 6.3 First-boot admin, then real staff accounts

      `directus-admin-bootstrap-password` (§3). Sign in once, then:
- [ ] Provision real staff as Directus users with the **Staff** role (from the applied schema
      snapshot), authenticating via the Google OIDC client from §6.1 — no self-registration
      (`AUTH_GOOGLE_ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION=false`), an admin creates each user's Directus account

Directus, which handles its own native Google OIDC — no oauth2-proxy needed for that surface).
Directus talks to its own database on the shared Cloud SQL instance over private IP directly (same
VPC, no proxy). New `crm.<internalDomain>` DNS record.

**Schema:** committed `packages/portal/deploy/directus/schema.yaml` — not hand-written. I built all
11 collections from `docs/people-hub-schema.md` against a real local Directus container via its
API, then exported it with `directus schema snapshot`, and verified it applies cleanly to a fresh
instance. `apply-permissions.mjs` (schema snapshots don't cover roles/permissions) creates the
Staff/Coach/Guardian roles, verified end-to-end including the Guardian policy's relational
`$CURRENT_USER`-scoped filters.

## Significant finding — please read

Building that verification surfaced something that affects the core rationale for choosing
Directus at all: **Directus 12's license (MSCL) gates custom/relational permission rules — exactly
what the Guardian policy's "see only your own minor" filtering depends on — behind a paid
Enterprise license.** Confirmed hands-on: a fresh, unlicensed Directus 12.3.1 instance rejects that
kind of permission with `403 custom_permission_rules_enabled is a restricted resource`; the
identical call succeeds on Directus 11.17.4 (still BSL-licensed, free). I've pinned the compose
file to `11.17.4` with a loud comment against bumping to v12+ without re-checking this, and written
up the full story in `docs/manual-setup.md` §6. Worth deciding consciously whether staying on 11.x
long-term is acceptable or whether Enterprise licensing needs to be budgeted for.

## Other things worth knowing

- `medical_profiles.person_id` reverted from "doubles as the primary key" to a normal `id` + unique
  `person_id` FK — Directus's relations API refuses to attach a relation to a field flagged as a
  collection's primary key. `docs/people-hub-schema.md` updated to match.
- Found and documented a real operational gotcha: after `directus schema apply` (a CLI process),
  the running server's schema cache is stale until restart — confusing 403s otherwise.
- All temporary local containers/network used for verification were torn down; nothing left
